summary_of_pdf: Transcript of an automated telephonic routing message dated October 15, 2026, documenting an unsuccessful attempt to contact the Houston-area telephone number (346) 426-5064 due to a capacity-exhausted voicemail receptacle.
attorneys_comments: From an evidentiary standpoint, this recording constitutes admissible proof of a good-faith attempt to communicate with an opposing party, witness, or counsel. Within the Southern District of Texas, Local Rule 7.1 mandates strict compliance with conferral requirements prior to filing most motions. A documented failure to reach opposing counsel due to an unmaintained or evasive telephonic system (e.g., a full voicemail box) fortifies our position that conferral was diligently attempted but rendered impossible by the recipient's administrative dereliction. It may also serve as circumstantial evidence of evasion if the recipient is a defendant avoiding service or a witness dodging a subpoena. While insufficient to establish formal service of process under FRCP 4, it is highly probative for motion practice concerning discovery disputes or requests for alternative service.
recommended_next_steps: Secure the native audio file with its metadata intact to ensure admissibility under Federal Rule of Evidence 901. Promptly transmit a follow-up communication via electronic mail and certified U.S. Mail, explicitly referencing this failed telephonic attempt, to unequivocally satisfy the meet-and-confer obligations of FRCP 37 and SDTX Local Rule 7.1.
